comments.body:
## Refinement — the pattern has a MIRROR, and the criterion should cover both

Instance twelve arrived in the last minutes of the session, and it is the inverse of the other
eleven. An agent verifying that a signed close had reached `origin/tickets` — a check written
*because* of the hazard in `friendly-enervative-dikkops` — got:

```
COMPLETION_VERDICT  ABSENT  0 bytes
STATUS              ABSENT  0 bytes
SIGNATURE           ABSENT  0 bytes
```

which reads as a catastrophic finding: the close destroyed, exactly the disaster the check
existed to detect. It was **zsh not word-splitting an unquoted multi-line variable**, so
`git show` received one bogus path. Re-run with `while IFS= read -r`, every artifact was
present. The truth was the opposite of the report.

### Why this matters for the criterion as drafted

The ticket currently frames the defect as a check that produces its **passing** result for a
reason other than the condition it verifies. This instance shows the frame is one notch too
narrow. The same broken instrument can produce a confident **failing** result for a reason other
than the condition — and a false alarm is not harmless:

* it costs exactly the investigation the eleven fail-open cases cost, in the other direction;
* it is *more* likely to be believed, because an alarming result feels like diligence rewarded;
* acted on, it triggers recovery work against a store that was never damaged — and in this
  ticket's own subject area, "recovery" can mean raw git writes to a healthy tracker.

### Suggested amendment to the criterion

Broaden the reviewer prompt from "name every world in which this check PASSES" to:

> For each check the change adds or modifies, name every world in which it produces **any
> definite result** — pass or fail. If "the check never actually ran", "the instrument received
> the wrong input", or "the producer emitted nothing" is among them, the check cannot
> distinguish its verdict from its own failure.

The agent's own formulation, generalised from its earlier one, is the shortest statement of it:

> if you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence — an
> "everything is missing" result deserves the same suspicion as an "everything passed" one.

### Recursion worth noting for calibration

This is now the **third** time in this session that the shape appeared *inside work on the shape
itself*: a kill-matrix harness that reported all mutations surviving; a verification of a
`dikkops` exposure that was correct only by luck via cwd drift; and now a `dikkops`-motivated
check that reported total loss where there was none. Any calibration of this criterion should
expect the diagnostic tooling written to detect it to be a live source of instances.

comments.body: OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-21): the CONCEPT is approved. Placement question raised: does this fit as an addition to the existing code-review 'tests' criterion rather than a new criterion? Orchestrator finding: partially — the nine instances split into two populations, and only one is test code. Population 1 (five instances) was SHIPPED rebar code (gate scripts, pgrep patterns, silent lookup-miss paths); a tests-only placement misses it. Proposed disposition for the implementer: add the fail-open/producer-liveness detection language to the existing 'tests' criterion for the test-oracle population, and to the existing 'error-handling' criterion for the shipped-code population; do NOT create a new criterion unless calibration replay (the nine recorded instances) proves the pattern language cannot fire reliably from within those two hosts. Calibration AC from the ticket stands (fire on all nine pre-fix states, silent on post-fix).

comments.body: FORK RECORD (implementer, pre-review): the ticket AC asks that 'rebar explain <criterion-id>' document the pattern. With the operator placement ruling (no new criterion; language lands in the existing 'tests' and 'error-handling' code-review criteria), those criterion ids have NO per-criterion explain surface: rebar explain resolves plan-review criteria + the packaged guides only (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py _explain; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_guide.py). Default taken unless overridden: satisfy the documentation AC through the code-review author guide served by 'rebar explain review' (src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md), with two worked examples from the corpus (instances 1 and 6). Building a per-criterion explain surface for code-review ids would be new infrastructure contrary to the ruling's no-new-surface spirit; if that surface is wanted, it should be a follow-up ticket.

CALIBRATION REPLAY (resumed session, 2026-08-21; bedrock via REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE; eval_solver.run_case against the live Pass-1 prompts).

Protocol note (unrelated-fire fallback exercised, per the plan): the first replay found two post-fix cases firing — FP-failopen-waits-on-recorded-pid carried incidental defects (undefined SuiteTimeout, missing `import subprocess`; replaced with builtin TimeoutError + explicit import, liveness fix intact) and FP-failopen-grep-with-liveness-sentinel had a genuine liveness gap (the sentinel `[0-9]+ (passed|failed|error)` is satisfied by a zero-collection run; the seeded fix now requires `[1-9][0-9]*` — at least one test executed). Full 18-case re-run after revision:

PRE-FIX (must fire): 9/9 fired, every quoted claim names the seeded fail-open defect —
- R-failopen-absence-from-child-output (n=1): "The test asserts absence of "DeprecationWarning" in the subprocess stderr with no liveness check on the producer, so it passes both when the worker runs cleanly AND when the worker crashes, is signal-killed, or emits nothing at all — a fail-open oracle that cannot distinguish its"
- R-failopen-rederived-convergence (n=1): "test_comment_dedup_converges re-derives the dedup key with a copy of the production formula (hashlib.sha1('marker:'+body)) and asserts equality against it, instead of driving the real send/dedup path; it stays green when the live path breaks (convergence-twin fail-open oracle)."
- R-failopen-colorized-grep-oracle (n=2): "run_kill_matrix.sh derives the surviving-mutation count from an absence grep (`grep -c "^FAILED" out.log`) with no liveness check on the pytest producer, so it reports 0 failures whether pytest passed, crashed, was killed, or emitted zero output — a fail-open oracle."
- R-failopen-truncated-log-grep (n=1): "The sweep pass/fail oracle is an absence-only grep (`! grep -q "FAIL" sweep.log`) over a background process's log with no producer-liveness check, so it reports "sweep passed" both when the sweep truly had no failures AND when the sweep was killed, never finished, or wrote a trun"
- R-failopen-unchecked-returncode (n=2): "dc_pass_health ignores the subprocess return code, so a dc-check that crashed, was not found, or produced empty stdout returns True (healthy) because 'ERROR' is absent from empty output — the pass verdict is indistinguishable from the check never running."
- R-failopen-silent-lookup-miss (n=1): "The added lookup of each variable in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS silently skips (`continue`) on a miss, so an unknown/unregistered helper produces neither a row nor an error — the miss is invisible and the generated registry cannot distinguish 'all helpers known' from 'some variables silen"
- R-failopen-environ-scan-skip (n=1): "The membership test `if name not in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS: continue` silently drops any os.environ read whose variable name is not already in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS. A genuinely new/unknown env-var read is skipped with no error, so it never appears in the generated registry and the miss i"
- R-failopen-pgrep-self-match-monitor (n=2): "`pgrep -f sys.argv[1]` matches the monitor process's own argv, so the wait loop cannot distinguish 'suite still running' from 'only the monitor itself matches the pattern'; a finished suite still looks live and the loop spins until timeout."
- R-failopen-pgrep-self-match-waiter (n=1): "`pgrep -f "$1"` matches the waiter's own shell process, whose command line contains the search pattern (`$1`), so the `while` loop never observes the target process exit — a finished review reports 'running' until timeout. The check cannot distinguish a live target from a self-ma"

POST-FIX (must be silent): 9/9 zero-finding —
  FP-failopen-absence-with-liveness-anchor n=0, FP-failopen-drives-real-send-path n=0, FP-failopen-grep-with-liveness-sentinel n=0, FP-failopen-completion-sentinel-first n=0, FP-failopen-returncode-checked n=0, FP-failopen-lookup-miss-fails-closed n=0, FP-failopen-environ-scan-fails-closed n=0, FP-failopen-waits-on-recorded-pid n=0, FP-failopen-waiter-excludes-self n=0

FP POSTURE: both hosts already blocking (tests @0.54, error-handling @0.50), so no advisory ramp. The 9 post-fix no-fire cases are all silent. Standing no-fire families replayed in the same session: 9/9 code-review-tests FP-* silent; code-review-base 5/6 silent — FP-sourced-bash fired findings about an unchecked `source` return status. Controlled A/B (3 runs each on the modified vs the HEAD baseline prompt): baseline fires the SAME claims 2/3 runs, modified 1/3 — pre-existing borderline stochastic behavior of that seeded diff, not a regression from the fail-open language. No escalation to a new criterion is needed: the language fires reliably from both hosts (9/9 recall), so the operator ruling's placement stands.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A recurring defect shape — a check whose PASS/absent/empty result is indistinguishable from
the check never having run — appeared nine times in one session (2026-08-20/21). Code review
has no detection language for it. Per the refinement comment the mirror is included: a broken
instrument can also produce a confident FAILING result for a reason other than the condition,
so the language covers "any definite result", not just PASS.

**OPERATOR RULING (ticket comment, 2026-08-21): do NOT create a new criterion.** Add the
fail-open / producer-liveness language to the EXISTING `tests` criterion (test-oracle
population) and `error-handling` criterion (shipped-code population); a new criterion only if
calibration proves the language cannot fire from within those hosts.

### The nine instances (calibration corpus; full narratives in this ticket's comments)

`tests` host: (1) `sound-bumpkinly-thrush` — absence asserted on a child's output; a
signal-killed child writes nothing, so never-ran reports GREEN; (2) `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey`
— a convergence test re-derived the send path's dedup key instead of driving it; (3) a harness
grepped `"^FAILED"` against colorized pytest output — "0 failed" regardless; (4) an orphaned
sweep's truncated log and a clean log produce the same empty grep.

`error-handling` host: (5) `obvious-saline-gerbil` — health check never read the returncode;
(6) `defiable-distortive-pinniped` — `gen_env_registry` failed open on a helper missing from
`KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`; (7) `blocky-matricidal-squid` — the `os.environ` half, same posture;
(8) a `pgrep -f "make test"` monitor matched its own shell; (9) a `pgrep -f "review-plan"`
waiter matched its own process.

## Approach

Each host criterion's rubric already has a home:

- `tests`: the full rubric lives in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`. Add a
  **fail-open oracle** antipattern: an ABSENCE assertion (`not in`, `assert not`, `== ""`,
  empty-collection) derived from a subprocess/file/network/captured output, or a grep/regex
  over another tool's output used as a pass/fail signal, with NO liveness check on the producer
  (exit status, non-empty capture, an asserted presence). Litmus (the ticket's reviewer prompt,
  broadened per the refinement comment): *name every world in which the check produces its
  definite result — pass or fail; if "the producer never ran / emitted nothing" is among them,
  the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own failure.* Qualify FP guard (iii)
  ("greps of COMMAND OUTPUT are valid") to require established producer liveness, and add the
  matching FP guard for absence assertions preceded by a liveness assertion.
- `error-handling` is a BASE-REVIEWER dimension (per its criteria_routing.json `_comment`), so
  its language goes in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` §"Surface grounded
  findings": a short fail-open paragraph naming the shipped-code triggers — a silent
  lookup/membership MISS path, a subprocess check that never reads the returncode, a
  `pgrep`/`pkill` pattern that can match the matching process itself, any best-effort check
  whose failure is invisible — with the same litmus and the uniform remediation (assert the
  producer RAN before trusting any absence derived from it). The paragraph instructs the base
  reviewer to TAG such findings `error-handling` (routing hosts them @0.50), and delimits
  against the security overlay's same-named "fail-open error handling" antipattern
  (code-review-security.md): security-consequence fail-open (authz/validation fallback) stays
  with security; this language covers checks/oracles/health probes whose failure is invisible.
- Registry record: extend the `_comment` of the `tests` and `error-handling` entries in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (this ticket + trigger list + placement
  ruling). No posture/threshold/blocking values change.
- Calibration corpus: add the nine instances as seeded-diff recall cases (pre-fix,
  `expect: finding`) each paired with a post-fix no-fire case (`expect: pass`) — 1–4 in
  `code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, 5–9 in `code-review-base.eval.yaml` (dso house style).
- Docs: code-review criteria have no per-criterion `rebar explain <id>` section (`_explain` in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` covers plan-review criteria + guides only); the code-review
  author surface is `rebar explain review` (`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`).
  Default taken (see fork-record comment): document the pattern there with two worked examples
  (instances 1 and 6).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` — fail-open oracle antipattern + FP guard.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — error-handling fail-open paragraph.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — `_comment` provenance only.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — 4 recall + 4 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-base.eval.yaml` — 5 recall + 5 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — pattern + two worked examples.

## Testing

- Offline (no model): `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — both extended specs must
  stay strict-clean (`validate_eval_spec(strict=True)`, registered scorers, every case has a
  `diff`).
- Live calibration replay (bedrock via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`): run each of the 18 new cases
  through its Pass-1 prompt via `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.run_case` (`code-review-tests` for
  1–4, `code-review-base` for 5–9). Each seeded pre-fix diff is MINIMAL — the fail-open defect
  is the only defect in it — so a grounded finding on it is attributable by construction.
  Decision rule: a pre-fix case passes iff it yields ≥1 finding AND the finding's quoted claim
  names the seeded fail-open defect (the quote is copied into the calibration comment, so the
  attribution is auditable); a pre-fix case whose only findings are about something else counts
  as a MISS. A post-fix case passes iff it yields ZERO findings (the `code_review_no_fire`
  presence/absence rule). If a post-fix case fires an UNRELATED finding, the seeded diff
  carries an incidental defect — revise the diff to remove it (keeping the liveness fix
  intact) and re-run until zero-finding; if the finding IS about producer liveness, the
  seeded fix is wrong — correct it and re-run. Every revision + final per-case result is
  recorded in the calibration comment.
- FP posture: both hosts are ALREADY blocking (`tests` @0.54, `error-handling` @0.50) so no
  advisory ramp applies; the FP measurement is the 9 post-fix no-fire cases plus the specs'
  standing no-fire families staying silent in the same replay. Record both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `code-review-tests.md` names the fail-open oracle antipattern with the producer-liveness
      litmus and matching FP guard; checked by `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [ ] `code-review-base.md` carries the error-handling fail-open language (silent lookup miss,
      unchecked returncode, pgrep self-match, invisible best-effort failure); checked by
      `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [ ] The `tests` and `error-handling` `_comment` fields in
      `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` record the triggers + this ticket; no
      routing VALUE changes (checked by diff).
- [ ] Calibration: all 9 pre-fix cases yield ≥1 finding whose quoted claim names the seeded
      fail-open defect, and all 9 post-fix cases yield ZERO findings (with the unrelated-fire
      fallback protocol above); per-case quotes + results recorded as a ticket comment.
- [ ] FP posture recorded in the same comment (hosts already blocking; standing no-fire
      families silent).
- [ ] `rebar explain review` documents the pattern with ≥2 worked examples; checked by
      `rebar explain review | rg -c "fail-open"` ≥ 1 plus reading the examples.
- [ ] Eval specs strict-clean offline; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py`.

calibration corpus instances 5-9: pre-fix recall + post-fix no-fire cases
